rows.uncertainty: Percentages do not all fit the 240 denominator: 100/240 is [41.7%] (printed 41.6%) and 25/240 is [10.4%] (printed 10.3%); printed percentages sum to [99.8%]. The three grade counts sum to [240], so the abstract implies no patient improved less than 25% or not at all; no grade below 25% is reported. Unit is the patient though lesions were treated; the number of lesions per patient and how a per-patient grade was formed are not in abstract. No control or untreated lesions, so improvement cannot be separated from natural change or seasonal tanning. Assessors, blinding and the scale are not in abstract. A single 2-month visit after one session; durability is not tested, far short of 6 months. Mean IGH duration '2.64 +/- 0.36 years' has [an unusually narrow spread for 240 patients]. Conclusion 'might be very effective without any considerable side effects' is not backed by an adverse-event count in the abstract. Publication metadata: PubMed status is still 'aheadofprint' with no pages, and Crossref lists no volume or issue, so [the article may never have appeared in a print issue]; no correction or retraction notice is linked in Crossref.
rows.citation: Goldust M, Mohebbipour A, Mirmohammadi R. Treatment of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis with fractional carbon dioxide lasers. J Cosmet Laser Ther 2013 May 8 (online ahead of print)
